title: Set up Rust
summary: Install Rust, find your way around a Cargo project, and run your first example.

title: Values, functions, and control flow
summary: Write functions, choose between cases, and handle numbers that reach their limits.

title: Ownership, places, and moves
summary: Learn what moves, what gets copied, and when a borrow is enough.

title: Borrowing and reborrowing
summary: Use shared and exclusive references, and see when a borrow ends.

title: Strings, slices, and collections
summary: Work with UTF-8 text and choose when collections should own or borrow data.

title: Structs, enums, and program states
summary: Represent your data with structs and enums, and reject invalid states.

title: Errors as part of the interface
summary: Use Option, Result, and useful error messages to handle different kinds of failure.

title: Stage build: the first event counter
summary: Build a working event counter with loops, matching, and borrowed text.

title: Lifetimes describe relationships
summary: Connect borrowed results to their inputs without trying to extend the life of data.

title: Traits and reusable interfaces
summary: Use standard traits, associated types, and static or dynamic dispatch.

title: Iterators and closures
summary: Follow iterator items, closure captures, and errors through your code.

title: Stage build: a bounded streaming library
summary: Build a library that parses records as it reads them and limits buffer growth.

title: Cargo, modules, and dependency boundaries
summary: Understand packages, modules, features, and the dependencies your program builds.

title: Tests, compiler errors, and verification tools
summary: Test expected behavior and failures, then use compiler checks and Clippy to catch more mistakes.

title: Interior mutability and shared ownership
summary: Choose between reference counting, runtime borrow checks, and locks.

title: Threads, Send, and Sync
summary: Move or borrow data across threads, then handle completion and failure.

title: Channels, locks, and shutdown
summary: Pass work through channels, protect shared data, and shut down without deadlocks.

title: Atomics and memory ordering
summary: Use atomic counters and understand why sharing other data needs more than a flag.

title: Futures before runtimes
summary: Learn how polling and wakeups work before adding an async runtime.

title: Tokio tasks, blocking, and cancellation
summary: Run Tokio tasks, limit queued work, and handle blocking calls and cancellation.

title: Pin and async traits
summary: Learn what pinning protects and how to return futures through a trait object.

title: Stage build: process records with async tasks
summary: Send records through a bounded queue and keep one task in charge of the counts.

title: Unsafe boundaries and soundness
summary: Review a small unsafe function, explain its safety rules, and check it with Miri.

title: Measure performance and resource use
summary: Measure speed and memory use before changing how the program works.

title: Stable Rust and work in progress
summary: Tell stable features apart from nightly experiments and plans that may change.

title: FFI, serialization, and public contracts
summary: Define ownership, data formats, and errors when calling code outside Rust.

title: Capstone: ship Fieldnotes
summary: Combine the parser and reader into a command-line tool you can install and use.

title: Release, maintain, and keep learning
summary: Check compatibility, release a reproducible build, and keep the course up to date.
